verses.text: Around then, Herod the ruler of Galilee heard reports about Jesus.
He told his servants, “This is John the Baptizer, back from the dead. That’s why these powers are working through him.”
Herod had arrested John, chained him up, and locked him away because of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife.
John had told him, “It’s not lawful for you to have her.”
Herod wanted to kill John, but he feared the crowd. They considered John a prophet.
At Herod’s birthday party, Herodias’s daughter danced in front of the guests and pleased him.
So he swore an oath to give her whatever she asked for.
Her mother coached her, and she said, “Bring me John the Baptizer’s head right here on a platter.”
The king was upset, but because he’d sworn in front of the dinner guests, he ordered it done.
He sent someone to the prison to behead John.
John’s head was brought in on a platter and given to the young woman. She carried it to her mother.
John’s disciples came, took his body, and buried him. Then they went and told Jesus.
When Jesus heard the news, he left by boat for a quiet, deserted place by himself. The crowds heard and followed him on foot from the towns.
Jesus stepped out and saw a huge crowd. His heart went out to them, and he healed their sick.
When evening came, his disciples said, “This place is deserted, and it’s already late. Send the crowds away so they can get food in the villages.”
Jesus told them, “They don’t need to leave. You give them something to eat.”
They replied, “All we’ve got here is five loaves and two fish.”
He said, “Bring them here to me.”

He told the crowds to sit down on the grass. Then he took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed them, broke the loaves, and handed them to the disciples. The disciples passed the food around.
Everybody ate and had enough. They gathered twelve baskets full of leftovers from the broken pieces. 🍞
About five thousand men ate, besides the women and children.
Right away, Jesus had his disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side, while he sent the crowds home.
After sending the crowds off, he went up the mountain alone to pray. Evening came, and he was still there by himself.
By then the boat was far out on the sea, getting knocked around by waves. The wind was against them. 🌊
During the fourth watch of the night, Jesus came toward them, walking on the sea.
When the disciples saw him walking on the water, they panicked: “It’s a ghost!” They cried out in fear.
Jesus spoke to them right away: “Take heart! It’s me. Don’t be afraid.”
Peter answered, “Lord, if that’s really you, tell me to come to you on the water.”
Jesus said, “Come!” Peter stepped out of the boat and walked on the water toward him.
But when Peter noticed how strong the wind was, fear took over. He started sinking and shouted, “Lord, save me!”
Jesus reached out at once, grabbed him, and said, “You of little faith, why did you doubt?”
They climbed into the boat, and the wind stopped.
Everyone in the boat worshiped him: “You really are God’s Son!”
After crossing over, they came to the land of Gennesaret.
The people there recognized Jesus and sent word all through the surrounding area. They brought him everyone who was sick.
They begged just to touch the edge of his robe. Everyone who touched it was healed.
